mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which positively impacts corporate earnings and drives up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day S&P 500 returns are not positively correlated with GDP growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when UNRATE drops below 3.5% more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate increases while unemployment decreases, it indicates tightening monetary policy, which can negatively impact equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5% and UNRATE decreases by 0.2pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases where FEDFUNDS and UNRATE move as described.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production suggests increased economic activity, which can lead to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days during an economic expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not higher than average during periods of industrial production growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not positively correlated with PAYEMS growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which can lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when HOUST exceeds 1500 more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales increase and federal funds rate is low, it indicates strong consumer demand and easy monetary conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases where RSAFS and FEDFUNDS move as described.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate during the early stages of an economic recovery signals improving labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not higher than average during periods of UNRATE decline in early recovery (t-test p > 0.05).
